question: The mode and median of a data set is 89.7 and 32, respectively. What is the mean of the data set? (Use empirical formula.)
solution: __Shortcut Trick__ Apply the **Empirical Formula**: **Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean**. Substitute the given values: 89.7 = 3 × 32 − 2 × Mean. 89.7 = 96 − 2 × Mean ⇒ 2 × Mean = 96 − 89.7 = 6.3. Mean = 6.3 ÷ 2 = 3.15. **∴ The correct answer is 3.15.** **__Alternate Method__** **Given:** **Mode** of the data set = 89.7 **Median** of the data set = 32 **Formula Used:** The relationship between **Mean**, **Median**, and **Mode** is given by the **Empirical Formula**: **Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6fc02f01c841558bd98f0e58fd097095249919a5e928f8a47f85c8f834605f76.png] **Calculations:** ⇒ 89.7 = 3 × 32 − 2 × Mean ⇒ 89.7 = 96 − 2 × Mean ⇒ 2 × Mean = 96 − 89.7 ⇒ 2 × Mean = 6.3 ⇒ Mean = 6.3 ÷ 2 ⇒ Mean = 3.15 **∴ The correct answer is 3.15.** **__Additional Information__** Empirical Formula Application This formula is used for **moderately skewed** distributions. For a perfectly **symmetrical distribution**, Mean = Median = Mode.
